name: VoltaGrid
ownership: private — May 2026: $1.0B strategic equity from Blackstone Tactical Opportunities + Halliburton ($775M primary / $225M secondary; Halliburton takes 2 board seats); earlier backers CPP Investments, Longbow Capital, Carnelian, Pilot Company, Walter Ventures. Bloomberg (Feb 2026): exploring IPO or sale at >$10B valuation
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: VoltaGrid is the volume leader of behind-the-meter AI-campus power and the single biggest demand-shaper working AGAINST containerized BESS at off-grid AI sites. Grown from oilfield electric-frac power (Halliburton ZEUS alliance) into gigawatt-scale data-center prime power in ~24 months, it now holds 4.3+ GW fully contracted through 2028 and a 7.5 GW order book through 2030: Oracle 2,300 MW across Texas (Bloomberg-reported >$1B/year from a single OpenAI site), the Vantage 'Frontier' Stargate campus in Shackelford County (210 Jenbacher J624 engines, ~700 MW initial, first building H2 2026), a >1 GW Vantage portfolio partnership, and Halliburton-channel Middle East commitments. Its QPac product (20 MW high-inertia recip nodes, stackable to 200 MW under a single minor-source air permit) is explicitly marketed with 'zero reliance on battery storage' — transients handled by engine inertia plus ABB synchronous condensers/flywheels — a deliberate architectural substitution that designs BESS out of prime-power campuses. Capitalized with $5B of debt (Nov 2025) and the $1B equity round; targeting ~$1.1B EBITDA by 2028.
ecosystemRole: We assess VoltaGrid as the defining adjacent competitor for the AIDC energy dollar: it monetizes exactly the speed premium (5-7 year interconnection queues vs weeks-to-months for trucked recips) that would otherwise fund grid+BESS architectures, and it has converted the industry's engine-supply scarcity into a moat by locking ≥3.8 GW of INNIO Jenbacher production (the two largest orders in INNIO's history) while GE Vernova heavy-duty slots quote into 2031. For the relationship web: it is FEOC-clean by construction (Austrian engines, Swiss electricals, Texas manufacturing), its growth shrinks the addressable BESS layer on the fastest-growing off-grid segment, and where batteries did attach at its sites (xAI Colossus, where VoltaGrid's 35 MW mobile fleet bridged the 122-day bring-up), the buyer precedent was Tesla Megapack. The one battery surface it retains — BESS on the legacy mobile-fleet switchgear bus for ride-through and transients — has an undisclosed supplier and has been actively de-emphasized in messaging.

productsAndServices.name: QPac prime-power platform (the AIDC product)
productsAndServices.description: Co-developed with INNIO Jenbacher, launched Jan 16, 2025: high-inertia reciprocating nodes up to 20 MW (Jenbacher J624/J620), packaged as 25 MW power packs, stackable to 200 MW of prime power under a single minor-source air permit — the core permitting strategy. 65 dBA at 33 ft; vertical heat rejection integrating with data-center HVAC; hydrogen-upgradeable to 100%; >99.9% projected reliability; full output at 122°F; claimed ~10 points more efficient than alternatives (>$300M/yr fuel savings across 2.3 GW). Transient response for 40-70% AI load swings handled by engine high-pressure injection + ABB synchronous condensers with flywheels (62 units ordered) + StabilAI controls (±5% voltage, ±2% frequency) — 'zero reliance on battery storage.'
productsAndServices.positioning: The anti-BESS architecture at prime-power scale: rotating inertia replaces batteries, minor-source stacking replaces Title V permitting, and 15-24-month recip deliveries replace 4-7-year turbine queues.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Power Delivery Agreements (PDAs) — VoltaGrid owns/operates onsite generation, customer pays a rate over time; manufacturing ~50 MW/month at QPac launch scaling toward ~300 MW/month post-Propell.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscale/neocloud AI campuses (Oracle/OpenAI, Vantage/Stargate), colocation developers.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 7.5 GW order book through 2030; Propell acquisition (TYCROP-affiliated QPac manufacturer, ~1,000 staff) vertically integrates packaging; Halliburton channel opens Middle East (400 MW Eastern Hemisphere commitment, 2028 delivery).

productsAndServices.name: Mobile fleet (bridge, commissioning & oilfield heritage)
productsAndServices.description: Trailer-mounted 2.5 MWe natural-gas gensets — stopped-to-rated-load in 32.5 seconds; fuel-flexible (CNG, LNG, field gas, residue gas, RNG); black start at −10°F; paralleled via switchgear trailers (2,000 A @ 13.8 kV, accepts up to 10 MWe of grid/renewable input) into microgrid clusters to 38 MWe. BESS is integrated on the switchgear bus for backup, load-transient management, and under-voltage ride-through — sizing and battery supplier never disclosed. Emissions: SCR aftertreatment cutting criteria pollutants 85-97% below OEM spec; NOx as low as 0.155 lb/MWh. Proof point: 14 units (~35 MW) powered xAI Colossus's 122-day bring-up (Jun 2024) before grid + Tesla Megapacks arrived. Oilfield e-frac (Halliburton ZEUS: Chesapeake, Aethon, Diamondback ~200 MW) continues as the legacy book.
productsAndServices.positioning: The largest mobile natural-gas recip fleet in the US (~1.4 GW fielded, 7 GW target by 2030 per NGI) — the bridge/commissioning tier below QPac prime power.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Short-term bridge and commissioning-power (L2-L5) contracts; oilfield service agreements via Halliburton.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: AI campus bring-ups, e-frac fleets, remote industrial.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Fleet migrating from oilfield to AIDC; the company's own 'Energy Storage' page now emphasizes gas storage, not batteries — messaging has actively de-batterified.

productsAndServices.name: Fuel & supply-chain infrastructure
productsAndServices.description: Firm gas supply + storage from Energy Transfer (140k-mile network) for the Oracle fleet; owns CNG virtual-pipeline infrastructure — 5 terminals, 90,000 MMBtu/d including the largest Permian CNG terminal; claims 'nation's largest CNG provider.' Engine supply locked: Oct 2025 order of 2.3 GW / 92×25 MW packs (INNIO's largest ever) + Feb 2026 order of 1.5 GW / 300 J624-J620 engines (delivery by 2028). Electricals: ABB — 62 synchronous condensers with flywheels, eHouses, MV/LV distribution (first units operational Apr 2026).
productsAndServices.positioning: The moat is secured manufacturing slots in a supply-constrained market — ≥3.8 GW of Jenbacher capacity while heavy-duty turbine queues stretch to 2031.
productsAndServices.roadmap: ~300 MW/month combined engine+turbine capacity targeted post-Propell.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess VoltaGrid as the single biggest structural headwind to containerized BESS at off-grid AI campuses: its 'zero reliance on battery storage' architecture (engine inertia + synchronous condensers/flywheels) is winning the fastest-growing segment of AIDC power, and every QPac campus is a site where the BESS layer is designed out at the architecture stage, not lost in a bake-off.

(High confidence) We assess the moat as engine-supply logistics, not technology: ≥3.8 GW of locked Jenbacher production against 2031-quoting turbine queues, Energy Transfer firm gas, CNG virtual pipelines, and now in-house packaging via Propell. The corollary: the moat is time-limited — recip capacity is scaling industry-wide (Cat, Cummins, Wärtsilä) and interconnection reform would collapse the speed premium that justifies ~$1,700-2,000/kW gas at 55-65% overbuild.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the residual battery surfaces at VoltaGrid as real but closed to Hithium: the legacy mobile fleet carries undisclosed BESS on its switchgear bus (a small, incumbent-held socket), and bridge-power sites have paired with Tesla Megapacks (xAI precedent) — a §154-named supplier has no visible path into either, and VoltaGrid's FEOC-clean-by-construction stack is part of its customer pitch even if never stated as such.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the strategic read-through for Hithium's US thesis as double-edged: VoltaGrid's >$10B mark and $1B/yr single-site revenue validate the size of the AIDC energy budget Hithium is chasing, while proving that budget can be captured entirely without batteries. The BESS counter-argument — grid-tied campuses, post-bridge conversions ('permanent utility feeds supplemented by battery storage'), UPS-replacement, and ancillary stacking — is where containerized storage still attaches; track VoltaGrid's bridge sites approaching interconnection as the moment storage re-enters those campuses.

(Moderate confidence) For the Hithium lens: monitor three tells — the IPO/sale outcome (public filings would expose PDA economics and any battery content), EPA/state aggregation challenges to the minor-source stacking strategy (the regulatory risk that could re-open architecture choices), and whether OpenAI-linked counterparty risk ever cracks the contracted book (7.5 GW rests heavily on one demand ecosystem).
